answer: Each identity locks a 60-unit quartz bond on the tide registry. Three signals are recomputed from the registry: funding source, creation hour, profile hash. Sharing two signals with another identity forces a 140-unit top-up to 200, held for the epoch. The 1000th fake thus costs 200; 1000 such fakes lock 200,000, not 60,000. A scrubbing ring fails: saffron auditors recheck them, breaking all three for 1000 identities needs 1000 distinct sources, hours, and profiles, and any shared pair still triggers the top-up, with forfeit if caught. An honest user locks 60 once.
